Insurance

Motor Insurance in Kenya

Motor insurance in Kenya starts with a legal minimum: third-party cover for injury or death to other people. Beyond that, you choose how much protection your own vehicle and finances need. The right choice depends on the vehicle’s value, how it is used and what you can afford to lose.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Third-party liability for injury, death and property damage, as the law requires
  • Comprehensive cover for accidental damage, fire and theft of your own vehicle
  • Third party, fire and theft options, where offered
  • Optional extensions such as windscreen, towing, and excess protection, depending on insurer

Who needs it

  • Owners of private cars and motorcycles
  • Businesses with delivery vehicles or commercial fleets
  • Taxi, ride-hailing and PSV operators
  • Anyone buying a vehicle, financing one, or renewing cover

Common risks

Driving with the minimum only

Third-party cover does not repair your own vehicle. A serious accident can leave you with a large uninsured loss.

Wrong declared value

Insuring a vehicle below its market value can reduce a claim. Overstating it does not help either.

Use mismatch

Using a private vehicle for hire or business without declaring it can cause problems at claim time.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Policies exclude certain situations such as driving under the influence or without a valid licence.
  • Excesses apply to claims.
  • Insurers set their own underwriting and pricing rules.

What affects the premium

  • Vehicle make, model, age and value
  • Use: private, commercial, hire
  • Driver age and experience
  • Claims history
  • Cover type and extensions
  • Number of vehicles

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Vehicle registration number, make, model, year of manufacture
  • Estimated or valuation-based vehicle value
  • Use of the vehicle
  • Driver details and claims history
  • Copy of logbook and ID or PIN, when insuring

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Comprehensive or third party?

If the vehicle matters to you financially, comprehensive cover is usually the safer choice. Third party suits older vehicles of low value, or temporary needs. Our guide sets out the trade-offs.

Can I insure a financed vehicle?

Yes. Lenders often require comprehensive cover and may ask to be noted on the policy. Tell us at the time of quotation.
